Sergio / Monica,

Below are concise answers you can share; I'm attaching a sanitized excerpt of our DR playbook and a network diagram for region mapping.

- RTO / RPO:
  * Hosted API: RTO ≤ 5 minutes for control-plane failover detection; warm standby routing achieved within 60–120 seconds for most regions. Logical RTO for in-flight request recovery depends on client retries; we recommend client-side idempotency. RPO: < 30 seconds for session state (in-memory KV caches flushed to persistent storage periodically); for customer data stored by Redwood (metadata, logs) RPO ≤ 5 minutes.
  * Dedicated deployments: RTO ≤ 10 minutes for orchestrated failover with dedicated capacity and cross-region replication enabled; RPO ≤ 5 minutes.

- Backups & retention:
  * Persistent metadata and configuration: snapshots every 6 hours, incremental DB-level backups every hour. Snapshots stored in primary region + cross-region replication to a secondary region (typically within the same cloud provider's paired region).
  * Object storage (user artifacts): versioned daily backups + lifecycle policy of 90 days for quick restore; cold archive available for >1 year on request.

- Regional failover:
  * Automated: health and latency probes trigger routing changes via our smart-router; for hosted customers we can route traffic to an alternate region automatically when latency/SLO breaches are detected. Typical automated failover time is 2–5 minutes for traffic re-routing, plus warm-up for model shards (additional 1–3 minutes depending on model size).
  * Manual: for Dedicated customers with strict data residency, we require a runbook-triggered cross-region activation; operator steps are documented. Expected total time 10–30 minutes depending on data sync.

Attachments:
- redwood-dr-playbook-snippet.txt (sanitized, incident steps, handoff points)
- network-diagram-westus.png (region map)
- sig_section_bcp_answers.pdf (draft answers formatted for SIG)

Let me know if you want any numbers tightened or if customer asks for SLA exceptions — that's legal/product.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear list. Please find our consolidated responses below and attached as a PDF (SIG_section_bcp_answers.pdf). I've also attached a sanitized excerpt of our DR playbook and a region/network diagram to help your reviewers.

Key points:
- Hosted API RTO: operational detection and control-plane failover within 5 minutes; warm standby routing typically completes within 60–120 seconds. RPO: <30s for runtime state; ≤5 min for persistent metadata.
- Dedicated RTO/RPO: RTO ≤10 minutes with cross-region replication enabled; RPO ≤5 minutes. Note: Dedicated with strict residency may require manual activation per contract.
- Backups: 6-hour snapshots + hourly incremental DB backups; cross-region replication; object storage daily versions with 90-day hot retention.
- Regional failover: automated routing available for Hosted customers with typical failover 2–5 minutes plus model warm-up; Dedicated customers use documented runbooks (10–30 min depending on dataset/model size).
